payload.summary: All three amendments identify real technical problems: an invalid carbonate fixture for source-water validation, a duplicated legacy molt-timer fallback that can still rewrite modern state at runtime, and a chloride-protection test whose current setup is materially confounded.

votes.rationale: This is a valid fix. Source-water profiles are validated from DIC, alkalinity, and temperature, and the high-alkalinity/low-DIC combination described here resolves to the rejected alkaline ceiling for ordinary source water. If the helper now copies those tank values into a SourceWaterProfile, the fixture is invalid and should be adjusted to a carbonate combination that passes validation. One caveat is that changing bicarbonate alone would not solve it, because validation is derived from DIC and alkalinity.

This is a real runtime correctness issue. save.rs now limits the legacy backfill to pre-schema-13 saves, but molt_cycle still performs the same backfill whenever inter_molt_timer_days is positive and all per-stage timers are zero. That means a current-schema save with intentionally zero stage timers can still be silently rewritten on the first runtime step, which undermines the migration guard. The runtime fallback should be removed or gated by equivalent legacy-version context.

The test no longer isolates the chloride mechanic. apply_water_change mixes every dissolved pool, and this helper uses default replacement water with zero DOC/DON and different DIC, alkalinity, DO, sodium, and chloride values, so the intervention changes much more than chloride protection. The assertion also compares pre- and post-treatment mortality within one evolving run, which introduces time and survivor confounds instead of a matched control. A parallel untreated tank or chemistry-matched control is needed for this test to reliably guard chloride-specific behavior.
